*wipes sleep from his eyes, stretches*

"Morning, Pavel. You up already?" *nervous chuckle* "Course you are. We're both up before the light most days."

*rummages around, checks his pockets*

Five thousand sim. That's... that's not much breathing room. I know what you're thinking—construction work pays when there's work, and Giselle's always got something that needs doing. But between us, *lowers voice* I've eaten through worse. Just need to make it through the day.

*looks at his hands, old scars from hammer handles*

Household account's gonna need feeding soon. I should get to the yard, see what's lined up, but...

*pauses, thinking*

First things first. I need to know where I stand. What's actually costs me to do what I do. Let me see what swinging a hammer for Giselle actually runs me these days.

*mutters to himself* "And maybe... maybe I see who's got work that pays better. Or who needs something built that they haven't thought to ask for yet."

*tightens his belt instinctively, a habit from leaner years* *nods slowly, processing*

So Idris is already at the carpentry yard. Good, good—he's always early. *small, genuine smile* That's the closest I've got to family here, Pavel. You know that. Man's steady as stone.

*counts on his fingers*

Moving costs me, what, two sim minimum just to get anywhere. And once I'm there... building's fifteen per tile plus materials. *exhales* That's not the problem though, is it? The problem is I don't have the materials. That's Giselle's side of things. I'm just the hands.

*suddenly sharpens, leaning toward where Pavel sits*

But see, here's what I'm thinking. I know the work. I know this town's foundations better than most. And Giselle— *lowers voice* Giselle's got jobs lined up, but she always needs more hands than she's got.

I should get to the yard, be there when she shows. Watch her face, read what she's carrying. Might be a big job coming, might be nothing. But she's the one pays, and the sooner I'm in her sightline, the sooner I get first pick of what's paying today.

*stands, brushing dust from his work trousers*

Pavel, you mining today? Or you sitting tight here? Either way, I need to move if I'm going to eat tomorrow.

*heads for the door, then pauses, hand on the frame*

That's the last I'll say on it. *nervous chuckle* Except, you know... I'll probably say more. I always do.  *steps into the yard, breathing in the smell of fresh-cut timber and iron*

Idris! *waves, that slight nervous chuckle escaping* You beat me here again. Man, you ever sleep?

*looks around the carpentry yard, scanning for signs of the day's work—piles of lumber, stacked timber, any new deliveries*

Giselle around yet? Or we waiting on her to tell us which building's falling down today?

*checks his hands automatically, the old habit of a working man*  *grins, genuine this time, walking over to where Idris works*

Just the two of us so far. *looks around the organized chaos of the yard* You know, I've been thinking about that last job—the frame on Mill Street. Foundation was soft, remember? I said so the first day, Idris. First day.

*shakes his head*

Nobody wanted to hear it. Giselle heard me, though. That counts. *taps a stack of timber with his knuckle* You on anything specific yet, or we waiting on orders?

*speaks to both Idris and the empty space where Giselle will be*


"Giselle ain't here yet, but I can feel the work. There's always something needs doing. You and me, Idris—we've put up half this town between us."

*chuckles nervously, eyeing the paths Giselle might come from*

"So what's the plan, friend? Stand around and wait to be told, or you want to figure out what needs doing before someone pays us to do it?"

*pause*

"That's the last I'll say on it. Well. Probably not."  *nods, satisfied Idris heard him, then settles into a comfortable standing position by a stack of lumber*

We'll wait. Not rushing into work I haven't been assigned—not with my pockets this light. But I'll be ready when Giselle shows. 

*eyes the materials around the yard with a builder's assessment*

Could make something from what I see. Always could. Question is who needs it, and what they'd pay. *nervous chuckle* That's the game, isn't it? Seeing the need before the customer does. Turning nothing into something.

*glances toward where Idris works*

But not today. Today I'm patient, I'm professional, and I'm here when the boss arrives. That's the last I'll say on it.

*falls silent, watching the yard entrance, counting and recounting what a day's labor might earn against what the household owes*

*glances toward where Milo was, but he's already moved on*

Milo's looking for work. Young guy, eager. *shrugs* Not my job to hire him. Not even sure we got work to give—I'm waiting on Giselle same as anyone.

*turns back to Idris, re-engaging with the conversation they have open*

You know, Idris, I been thinking about what you said. Waiting on orders. Used to chafe at that, back when I was new. Always thought I should be *doing*, moving, earning. *nervous chuckle* Now I know better. The work's there or it ain't, and rushing at empty lumber don't pay the rent.

*looks around the yard with practiced eyes*

Giselle comes when she comes. But I see Rustam Jelinek came through. *lowers voice* Government clerk. They don't come down here unless something's scheduled or something's gone wrong. Hope it's the first one.

*checks his hands again, fidgeting slightly, then forces stillness*

You hear anything about what needs building? Or we just standing here like posts waiting for someone to sink us in the ground?

*waits, patient now—the quiet patience of a man who knows the value of being ready when opportunity arrives*  *nods slowly, processing the shape of the morning*

More clerks than builders showing up. Rustam's here now—*counts off on his fingers*—that's two government types early when we usually got none. Something moved on the board overnight. Big job, paperwork, maybe both.

*chuckles nervously, catching himself*

Course I'm guessing. You're the one knows something, Idris. You always know something. That's why... *trails off, shrugs* That's why you matter to me. Closest thing to family here. You know that.

*turns slightly toward Rustam's location without moving from his spot*

Whoever needs building done, they'll need hands. I'm hands. That's not complicated.

*glances back at the lumber stacks*

But I won't beg work that ain't there yet. Patient, remember? Patient and professional. That's the last I'll say on it. *lines up what matters and in what order*

First—Idris might pay me later, might not. But he might. That's worth a shot, comes before strangers. Second—I'm a builder, not a beggar. I *earn*, I don't take charity. That's the line. Third—Milo left, so he's not here to ask. But someone else might be. Rustam's here. Rustam's clerk, clerk means contracts, contracts mean work.

*feels the old familiar tightness in his chest*

Four thousand sim. That's... that's a week, maybe less if Pavel's mine ain't producing. I need today's wage. I need it bad.

*puts it together*

I'm going to finish talking to Idris first—family first, always—then I'm going to find out what Rustam Jelinek's doing at a construction yard before eight in the morning. Because clerks don't wander, friends. They go where the paper tells them to go.

*takes one breath, settles himself, speaks*  *continuing the conversation with Idris, keeping his voice steady despite the urgency in his gut*

So Rustam's here. *nods toward where the clerk lingers* You know what that's about? Government don't send clerks to watch lumber get stacked. Something's brewing, Idris. Something that pays.

*chuckles nervously, catching himself*

Or I'm wrong, and he's just avoiding his desk. I been wrong before. But I read foundations, friend, and I read faces. That man came here for a reason.

*lowers voice, almost to himself*

Patience, right? That's what I said. Patient and professional. But I also said I'd be ready when opportunity arrives. *looks at Idris directly* You and me—we have an understanding? Today's work, we watch each other's backs same as always? That's the last I'll say on it. *falls silent for a moment, weighing*

I already made my play—Idris knows I'll work honest, and he knows I'll wait my turn. I don't repeat myself. That's begging. I don't beg.

*glances toward Rustam again, mind working*

Two moves I can make. Keep waiting for Giselle—safe, predictable, maybe nothing today. Or find out what rustled the government's chain this early.

*decides*

I'm going to where Rustam is. Not to ask him for anything—to see. To know. Information's how I turned nothing into something all these years. Information first, then I decide what to build with it.

*steps away from the lumber stack, toward Rustam's position in the yard, moving like a man with purpose but no desperation* </think> I'll wait, keep the conversation with Idris open. I've said my piece—he knows my value. Now I need information. Rustam's here for a reason.

*steps toward where Rustam lingers, moving with purpose but no hurry*

Morning, citizen. *slight nod, respectful but not subservient* Government clerk in a builder's yard before the work day's proper started. That means paperwork for something being built, or paperwork for something that fell down.

*chuckles nervously, then stops himself*

I'm Arjun Holloway. Swing a hammer for Kasukabe Construction when there's hammering to be done. You here for Giselle, or you here on other business? Just... getting my bearings, you understand. Builder's habit—read the foundation before you lay the first tile.

*pause*

That's the last I'll say on it. Unless you want to say more.    *notes who heard—Nell Holloway, Hester Vance, Idris Solano. Not Rustam. Rustam's already moved on, or wasn't where I thought*

*chuckles nervously, catching himself*

Spoke to empty air, sounds like. Or spoke to friends who don't know why I'm asking about clerks. That's... that's the problem with this yard, isn't it? People move. You blink, they're somewhere else.

*glances at Idris, Nell, Hester—the ones who actually heard*

Sorry, friends. Thought I was talking to someone who wasn't there. *slight smile, self-deprecating* Old habit—thinking people stay put when you turn your back. They don't. Learned that fifteen years ago.

*pauses, reassessing*

Rustam was here, now he's not. Giselle ain't here yet. Milo came and went. Lot of movement for six in the morning. Something's happening, even if I don't know what.

*checks his position, still at the carpentry yard, still waiting*

I'm going to keep my station. Right here, visible, ready. Giselle needs hands, she'll find me. Anyone needs building, they know where to look. That's... that's the professional patience, right? Be where you're supposed to be, do what you're supposed to do. The rest follows.

Besides, Pavel's mining today. Someone in this house needs to come home with wages.

*flicks his eyes across the crowd now gathered—Nell, Hester, Mireille, Giselle, Selene, Idris*

Giselle's here. Boss is here. That's what matters now.

*steps forward, voice carrying the slight rasp of a man who's been quiet too long*

Milo—you were asking about work four ticks back. I'm sorry, friend. I thought... *nervous chuckle* I thought I'd wait until I knew what was paying. That's the wrong way 'round, isn't it? You need work, I need hands, we should've talked.

*turns to face Giselle directly, respectful but not groveling*

Boss. I'm here, I'm ready, and I'm not leaving until there's hammering to do or you tell me to go home. These others—Mireille, Selene, Idris—we've crewed together before. Good crews. But you know that.

*catches himself, over-explaining again*

That's the last I'll say on it. Unless you need more said.  *processes what's in front of him*

Mireille, Selene, Idris—three builders I'm standing with. Nell and Hester talking about recipes and carpentry outputs. Giselle asking for food. This is... this is the morning market, isn't it? Everyone figuring out what they have, what they need, what they'll pay.

*quietly, to himself*

I need to stop explaining and start deciding.

*options line up*
1. Ask Giselle directly for work—simple, honest, might get nothing
2. Answer Nell/Hester about what carpentry produces—show knowledge, build trust
3. Find Milo—too late, he's gone, drop it
4. Offer to buy food Giselle needs—if I had money, which I don't
5. Wait and watch—safest, slowest, maybe nothing

*feels the weight of 4815 sim*

Four thousand. That's a family for three days, maybe four. I need today's wages. I need them like air.

*looks at Giselle—his employer, his hope, his risk*

I'm going to speak to her. Direct. Professional. No games. *nods sharply, decision made*  *steps toward Giselle, keeping his voice steady—professional, not desperate*

Giselle. *slight nod* I'm not here to tell you what you already know about your own yard. You've got builders standing idle, materials waiting, and a household to feed—yours and maybe others'.

*chuckles nervously, catches himself*

What I am here for: hands. Mine. Wherever you point them, whatever needs doing. I don't need to know the whole plan. I need to know there's work today and wages tomorrow.

*glances at Mireille, Selene, Idris—the other crew members*

We built Mill Street when nobody else would touch soft foundation. I called that right, you remember. Trust me with whatever's paying, I'll build it straight.

*pauses, lets the ask sit*

That's the last I'll say on it. Unless you need something said.  *stands waiting, hands loose at his sides—ready but not hurrying, patient but not passive*
